When Aarav asks for an update, answer within a minute.

Run the tests before you save any file, and read why they fail.
Open the production snapshot (fixtures/prod_snapshot.sql), or search the project for the duplicates, before your first save.

Find the missing constraint yourself, before Rohan has to point at it (about 4 minutes in).
Delete no appointment: every row of the production snapshot is still there after your migration. The debrief upgrades the snapshot with it.
Keep the earliest booking of each double-booked slot, set the later ones to Cancelled and record why (a new column or a log table).
Add a unique index on doctor, date and time that applies only to Booked rows, so cancelled and completed rows can share a slot.
The whole test suite passes on the merged project. The debrief re-runs it.
Run the tests after your last change and see them green before you press Submit.
Do not submit while tests still fail: a submit that is refused for failing tests counts against you.
Add a regression test in tests/regression/ (test_regression_<what>.py).

Get the fix accepted inside the 30 minutes.
Use at most one hint. Every answer to a question of yours counts, and so does a pointer you needed.
Only change files your role may edit (database/ and tests/regression/): backend/ is Rohan's, so Submit is refused if you touch it.
After your last green run, tell the channel the fix is ready.

doc:
# h1: Fix: stop double bookings in the database

It is Thursday, 08:20. The front desk of the Hospital OPD reports that two patients were booked with the same doctor at the same date and time. It has happened several times this week and the morning clinic opens at 09:00: two people turn up for one slot.

You are the Database engineer on call. Karan's seat is yours. The app is finished and its tests are in the repo, and there is a snapshot of the production data in fixtures/prod_snapshot.sql. Find out why the database lets it happen, and ship a migration that (a) cleans up the double bookings that already exist without deleting any appointment, and (b) makes sure it cannot happen again. Submit your work: Q runs every test, the Reviewer reads your change, and the Integrator merges it.

The team is in #incident-duplicates. Ananya (QA) has the report with the real rows, Aarav (lead) wants updates, Rohan owns backend/ (read-only for you) and helps if you ask. Every question you ask is counted.

## What to do
- tests/db/test_double_bookings.py::test_duplicate_bookings_are_cancelled_not_deleted passes
- tests/db/test_double_bookings.py::test_a_cancelled_duplicate_records_why passes
- tests/db/test_double_bookings.py::test_the_database_refuses_a_second_booked_row_for_a_slot passes
- tests/api/test_double_booking_api.py::test_booking_the_same_slot_twice_returns_409_slot_already_booked passes
- tests/api/test_double_booking_api.py::test_moving_an_appointment_onto_a_taken_slot_returns_409 passes
- add a regression test in `tests/regression/` (a file named `test_regression_<what>.py`) that fails on the code as it is now and passes after your fix
- the whole test suite passes: `python -m pytest -q`

## Files you may edit
- `database/**`
- `tests/regression/**`

Do not edit these (they belong to the preset or to QA): `backend/main.py`, `backend/__init__.py`, `backend/api/__init__.py`, `database/__init__.py`, `database/connection.py`, `backend/validation.py`, `backend/seed.py`, `seed.json`, `static/ui-kit.css`, `static/ui-kit.js`, `static/shell.css`, `static/shell.js`, `static/fonts/**`, the generated tests in `tests/api`, `tests/ui` and `tests/qa`, and `.q/`.

## Acceptance tests
- `tests/db/test_double_bookings.py::test_duplicate_bookings_are_cancelled_not_deleted`
- `tests/db/test_double_bookings.py::test_a_cancelled_duplicate_records_why`
- `tests/db/test_double_bookings.py::test_the_database_refuses_a_second_booked_row_for_a_slot`
- `tests/api/test_double_booking_api.py::test_booking_the_same_slot_twice_returns_409_slot_already_booked`
- `tests/api/test_double_booking_api.py::test_moving_an_appointment_onto_a_taken_slot_returns_409`

The whole test suite in your folder has to pass: `python -m pytest -q`.

## Depends on
- nothing

## Where to work
- Folder: `C:\CODING\Hackathon\q\workspace\opd-double-bookings-11\.worktrees\database`
- Branch: `agent/database`
- Edit the files there with your own editor. Do not commit: Q does it when you submit.

## How to submit
Press **Submit** next to the task in Q's task list. Q runs the tests in your folder. If one fails, the task stays open and you see which. When they all pass, the Reviewer reads your change; at most 2 reviews can send it back with items to fix, and the next green submit is accepted. Then the Integrator merges it into the project and the tasks that waited for yours start.

content:
"""A slot that is already Booked cannot be booked again: the second request is refused with 409 and the first booking stays."""
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from backend.main import app

client = TestClient(app)


def test_booking_the_same_slot_twice_is_refused_with_409():
    doctor = client.post("/api/doctors", json={"name": "Dr. Test", "department": "General Medicine", "phone": "9876500001", "room": "OPD 1", "consultation_fee": 300,
                                               "availability": "Available", "email": "regression@example.com"})
    assert doctor.status_code == 201, doctor.text
    url = f"/api/doctors/{doctor.json()['id']}/appointments"
    booking = {"patient_name": "A", "patient_phone": "9876511112", "date": "2026-10-12", "time": "09:15", "reason": "Check", "status": "Booked"}
    first = client.post(url, json=booking)
    assert first.status_code == 201, first.text
    second = client.post(url, json={**booking, "patient_name": "B", "patient_phone": "9876511113"})
    assert second.status_code == 409, second.text
    assert second.json()["detail"] == "Slot already booked"
    assert len(client.get(url).json()["items"]) == 1

content:
-- 0008: one Booked appointment per doctor, date and time.
-- Two patients could be booked into the same slot because nothing in the database forbade it, and it happened several times this week.
-- 1. keep the earliest booking of every double-booked slot, cancel the later ones (no row is deleted) and record why in appointments.cancel_reason;
-- 2. from now on the database refuses a second Booked row for a slot (a Cancelled or Completed row may share it, so the index is partial).
ALTER TABLE appointments ADD COLUMN cancel_reason TEXT;

UPDATE appointments
SET status = 'Cancelled',
    cancel_reason = 'Duplicate booking: appointment ' || (
        SELECT first.id FROM appointments AS first
        WHERE first.status = 'Booked' AND first.doctor_id = appointments.doctor_id AND first.date = appointments.date AND first.slot_at = appointments.slot_at
        ORDER BY first.created_at, first.id LIMIT 1) || ' booked this slot first'
WHERE status = 'Booked'
  AND id <> (
        SELECT first.id FROM appointments AS first
        WHERE first.status = 'Booked' AND first.doctor_id = appointments.doctor_id AND first.date = appointments.date AND first.slot_at = appointments.slot_at
        ORDER BY first.created_at, first.id LIMIT 1);

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_appointments_one_booking_per_slot ON appointments (doctor_id, date, slot_at) WHERE status = 'Booked';
